title: Phase 5 · Stage 16: Search with filter pipelines
summary: Build an advanced search from small Func<Book, bool> filters chosen at run time, plus a pluggable sort.

steps.title: Functions as values
body: Librarians want to search like this:
Every term is a **rule about a book**. A rule is a function from `Book` to `bool`, and C# can store functions in variables, lists and parameters as **delegates**:
filters.Add(b => b.Year > after);                     // "after=1940": the lambda captures 'after'
var found = library.Books.Where(b => filters.All(f => f(b)));   // every rule must say yes
- `Func<Book, bool>` takes a `Book` and returns a `bool`. `Func<A, B, R>` takes two, `Action<T>` returns nothing.
- A lambda can use variables from around it: it **captures** them. Each search builds fresh variables, so each filter remembers its own value.
- The sort is a function too: `Func<IEnumerable<Book>, IEnumerable<Book>> order = books => books.OrderBy(b => b.Year);` Pick one at run time, apply it at the end.
This is the **specification** idea: small rules, combined freely, instead of one giant method with a parameter for every possible question.

steps.explain: The lambda captured the **variable** `limit`, not its value at the time. By the time the query runs, `limit` is 6, so 7 fails.
A `Func<Book, bool>` holds the lambda; adding it to the list makes it one more rule every book must pass.

steps.prompt: What is the type of `b => b.AvailableCopies > 0` when it is stored in the filter list?
steps.explain: The last type argument of `Func` is the return type. `Action` delegates return nothing.

steps.title: The search command
prompt: New command `search <terms>`. Each space-separated term adds a rule; a book must pass **every** rule.
| `available` | at least one copy is in |
| `genre=<g>` | the genre is `g` (any case; a bad one prints the usual `Error: genre must be one of ...`) |
| `author=<text>` / `title=<text>` | the author / title contains the text, ignoring case |
| `after=<year>` / `before=<year>` | the year is greater / less than it (not a number: `Error: after needs a year`, `Error: before needs a year`) |
| `sort=title` / `sort=author` / `sort=year` | changes the order (default `title`; ties by title; ordinal). Anything else: `Error: sort by title, author or year` |
| `take=<n>` | at most `n` books (n at least 1, else `Error: take needs a positive number`) |

Store the rules in a `List<Func<Book, bool>>` and the sort in a `Func<IEnumerable<Book>, IEnumerable<Book>>`. Print the books, then `3 books found` (`1 book found`). With no match: `No books found.` `search` with no terms lists everything sorted by title. Add `search` to `help` after `find`.

require.message: Keeps the rules in a List<Func<Book, bool>>
Stores the sort as a Func<IEnumerable<Book>, IEnumerable<Book>>

hints: Split each term at the first `=` into a key and a value, then `switch (key)`. Each case adds one lambda: `filters.Add(b => b.Year > after);`.
The default sort is `books => books.OrderBy(b => b.Title, StringComparer.Ordinal)`; a `sort=` term replaces it with another lambda of the same type.
At the end: `IEnumerable<Book> result = order(library.Books.Where(b => filters.All(filter => filter(b))));` then apply `Take` when a limit was given.
